The photon energy is given by \(E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\). Using \(hc = 1240\ \text{eV·nm}\) and \(\lambda = 400\ \text{nm}\), we get \(E = 3.1\ \text{eV}\).

The steel tape expands with temperature. With coefficient \(\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{°C}^{-1}\) and \(\Delta T = 15\ \text{°C}\), the actual distance is \(d_{\text{actual}} = d_{\text{read}} (1 + \alpha \Delta T) = 35.794 \times 1.00018 = 35.800\ \text{m}\).

At noon on the summer solstice at latitude \(50^\circ\text{N}\), the solar declination is \(23.5^\circ\). The solar altitude is \(90^\circ - 50^\circ + 23.5^\circ = 63.5^\circ\), so the zenith angle is \(26.5^\circ\). The fraction of direct normal flux on a horizontal surface is \(\cos(26.5^\circ) = 0.8944\).

The equilibrium temperature is found from heat balance: \(m_{\text{coffee}} c_w (70 - T) = m_{\text{cup}} c_{\text{Al}} (T - 20)\). Using \(c_w = 4186\ \text{J/(kg·°C)}\) and \(c_{\text{Al}} = 900\ \text{J/(kg·°C)}\), we get \(T = 66.0\ \text{°C}\) (rounded to three significant figures).

The mean translational kinetic energy of an ideal gas molecule is \(\frac{3}{2} kT\). With \(k = 8.617 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{eV/K}\) and \(T = 293\ \text{K}\), the energy is \(0.0379\ \text{eV}\).

ANSWER: 3.1,35.800,0.8944,66.0,0.0379
